key_insight: A hybrid SCAPS-1D plus machine-learning workflow can efficiently screen multilayer perovskite solar-cell stacks and reveal the key layer properties that drive efficiency.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical design route for optimizing ETL, absorber, and HTL choices in high-efficiency, lead-free perovskite solar cells without exhaustive trial-and-error.
method: Trained an ML model on a representative subset to predict PCE for unexplored stacks.
Used SHAP analysis to identify the most influential descriptors and verify top candidates with full device simulations.
evidence_signal: Leave-One-Group-Out cross-validation showed reliable ranking via Spearman correlation, and the best verified devices reached 28.85% PCE (FTO/TiO2/Cs2AgBiBr6/NiO/Ag) and 28.62% PCE (FTO/SnO2/Cs2AgInBr6/NiO/Ag).
watch_item: The model’s screening power depends on the representativeness of the simulated training set, so transfer to new materials or fabrication conditions should be validated experimentally.
paper_title: Multilayer Screening of Double and Conventional Perovskite Solar Cells Using SCAPS-1D and Machine Learning: Optimization of ETL, HTL, and Absorber for High-Efficiency Architectures
